title: A multilevel sketch-and-solve method for overdetermined least squares problems
summary: Sketch-and-solve (SAS) is a very successful method to efficiently estimate the solution of heavily overdetermined large linear least squares problems. It uses random sketching to reduce the size of the problem, hence reducing the computational cost. Several authors have shown that averaging several solutions from SAS further improves the accuracy, which is measured by the residual associated to the approximate solution.
